desc: SS Fort Stikine was a Canadian-built cargo ship that exploded in Victoria Dock, Bombay (Mumbai) on 14 April 1944, causing the Bombay Harbour Explosion. The ship carried a mixed cargo including cotton bales, timber, and explosives. The explosion killed nearly 1,400 people and injured over 3,000, destroying 80 ships and causing massive damage to the dock area. The wreckage of the ship remains in the harbor floor. It is considered one of the largest non-nuclear explosions in history and devastated Bombay's port infrastructure during World War II.
fact: The explosion on 14 April 1944 killed nearly 1,400 people in Bombay Harbour · It was one of the largest non-nuclear explosions in history · The ship carried cotton, timber, and explosives as cargo · The explosion destroyed 80 ships and caused massive port damage

desc: HMIS Indus was a Grimsby-class sloop of the Royal Indian Navy that was sunk by Japanese aircraft on 6 March 1942 during World War II, near the Lakshadweep Islands. The ship was attacked while escorting a convoy in the Arabian Sea. Of the 161 crew on board, 83 survived and were rescued by other escort vessels. The wreck lies in the deep waters west of the Lakshadweep archipelago. It was one of the few Indian naval vessels lost to enemy action during World War II in the Indian Ocean.
fact: It was sunk by Japanese aircraft on 6 March 1942 near Lakshadweep · It was a Grimsby-class sloop of the Royal Indian Navy · Of 161 crew, 83 survived the attack · It was escorting a convoy in the Arabian Sea during WWII

desc: MV India Queen was a passenger cargo ship that sank off the coast of Goa in 2010. The ship was carrying construction material and supplies when it encountered rough seas during the monsoon season. The vessel went down approximately 30 nautical miles from the Goa coast near Aguada. All 11 crew members were rescued by the Indian Coast Guard before the ship sank. The wreck now lies at a depth of about 40 meters and has become an artificial reef attracting marine life, making it a potential site for recreational diving.
fact: It sank off the Goa coast in 2010 during monsoon rough seas · All 11 crew members were rescued by the Indian Coast Guard · The wreck lies at 40 meters depth and has become an artificial reef · It was carrying construction material when it went down

desc: SS Dome was a British cargo ship that shipwrecked near Sagar Island in the Hooghly River delta in the early 20th century. The ship was transporting jute and tea from Calcutta when it was caught in a severe cyclone and driven aground on the sandbars of the Sundarbans. The wreck became visible at low tide for many decades and became a landmark for local fishermen. Parts of the wreck have been salvaged over the years, but remnants remain buried in the shifting sands of the river mouth. It highlights the hazards of navigating the treacherous Hooghly River approaches.
fact: It wrecked near Sagar Island in the Hooghly River delta during a cyclone · It was carrying jute and tea from Calcutta · The wreck became visible at low tide for decades · It demonstrates the navigational hazards of the Hooghly River approach

desc: MV Princess of the Orient was a passenger ferry that capsized and sank off the coast of Karwar, Karnataka in 2023. The vessel was operating a coastal route along the western coast when it encountered severe weather conditions. The incident resulted in casualties and a major search and rescue operation by the Indian Coast Guard and Navy. The wreck lies at a depth of approximately 35 meters. The incident led to enhanced safety regulations for coastal passenger vessels. An investigation identified design stability issues contributing to the capsizing.
fact: It capsized off the Karwar coast of Karnataka in 2023 · It was a passenger ferry operating along the western coast · The wreck lies at 35 meters depth · The incident led to enhanced coastal vessel safety regulations
